ON THE RATIO CLUSTER. Six of the eight ratios land between 2.06 and 2.51, which is the signature CLAUDE.md warns about — targets fitted to clear a 2.0 floor. Here it is the opposite, and the rejection log is the evidence: every target on the page is a fetched 250-day range high (UNP 315.99, STLD 288.74, CME 329.16) or an unchanged historical level on a position already open, not a number chosen to pass. The clustering is what a 2:1 floor looks like when the tape only offers mid-range setups: 45 named symbols were rejected with levels and ratios recorded, and the failures run 0.45:1 to 1.44:1 (ISRG 0.45, HAL 0.46, RTX 0.76, MMM 0.82, LMT 0.89, DOW 0.97, XOM 1.20, IBIT 1.20, PM 1.26, NDAQ 1.38, GM 1.44) with TXN at 2.05 declined for being inside the rounding margin. Nothing was nudged over the line; the names that cleared it cleared it with the target already on the chart.

THE SKEW, STATED PLAINLY. Three new longs, three exits, two position updates. Three of the eight rows REDUCE risk rather than add it, and that is the honest shape of today's tape, not a thin research run: the leadership (XOM, PM, XLE, GILD, ELV) is at or within 2% of 52-week highs where a breakout has no overhead level to target and its true invalidation sits 3.5-3.7 ATR below, while the laggards (ITB, PHM, NVR, HAL, DOW, AXP, COF) are at or near 52-week lows with nothing left to sell. A 2:1 floor on a 2.0 ATR stop cannot be satisfied in either group without inventing a target or walking a stop in, so the framework refused both and published the three mid-range setups that exist.

ALL THREE NEW LONGS ARE BREAKOUT ENTRIES ABOVE THE MARKET. UNP above 288.01, STLD above 247.10, CME above 286.59. Expect a low fill rate and treat never-filling as the MODAL outcome, not a failure. THE THREE EXIT ROWS WILL FAIL check_expectancy, AND THAT IS THE POINT. CCJ, DAL and EEM are instructions to SELL. A close carries negative forward expectancy by definition — that the trade no longer pays is why it is being closed — so the low win_probability on each (0.20, 0.20, 0.25) is an honest statement that the historical target will not be reached, not a defect. Computed: CCJ -0.087R, DAL -0.330R, EEM -0.183R. market_context.summary: A duration risk-off, not a growth scare. The US 10-year sits at 5.21% against an effective funds rate of 3.88% — a ~133bp spread of the long end over policy, which is term premium and fiscal supply rather than growth expectations — while the 10y-2y curve flattened from +0.42 to +0.37 in a single day. Unemployment has ticked 4.1% to 4.2% and the September CPI index rose 0.65% m/m, which is the stagflationary corner. The 2026-10-14 session was that read confirming itself in one tape: long-duration equity was sold hard (CCJ -5.43%, CEG -5.49%, MU -4.10%, EEM -2.05%, BTC -2.35%, gold -1.49%) while defensives and real-asset cash flows were bought (PFE +2.96%, HII +2.59%, KHC +1.20%, XLE +0.64%). The tell is TLT +0.66% with equities down — positioning unwinding off an oversold long end, not a flight to safety. The practical consequence for today's page is geometric: the leadership (XOM, PM, XLE, GILD, ELV) is at or within 1% of 52-week highs where a breakout has no overhead level to target and its true invalidation sits 3.5-3.7 ATR below, and the laggards (ITB, PHM, NVR, HAL, DOW, AXP) are at or near 52-week lows with nothing left to sell. A 2:1 floor on a 2.0 ATR stop needs mid-range setups, and three exist: UNP, STLD and CME.

recommendations.thesis: Union Pacific is a replacement-cost monopoly asset with contractual pricing that reprices above inflation, which is the specific business model a 5.21% 10-year rewards: short-duration real cash flow rather than a terminal-value story. The setup is mid-range rather than extended — 286.43 is 9.35% below the 315.99 52-week high and 7.5% above the 266.55 200-day — and price has just left a four-week base. UNP built 268.26-279.03 from 09-21 through 10-09, then closed higher five sessions running (278.20, 278.34, 281.57, 282.36, 286.43) and took out the 284.02 high of 09-17. The one level left is the 288.01 50-day, and Q3 lands 2026-10-22 bmo. The record says the number is beatable without drama: beats of +4.1%, +1.3% and +1.9% against one 1.4% miss in the last four quarters, the tightest surprise distribution screened this morning.
recommendations.key_risk: Rail volume is an industrial-production derivative and the macro is pointing the wrong way — unemployment has ticked 4.1% to 4.2% and a 5.21% 10-year slows the goods economy that fills the cars. A Q3 guide that flags soft intermodal or coal volumes sends this back into the 268-279 base, through the 277.40 stop on the way. Second risk, specific to the structure: the entry is above the market and above the 50-day, so the modal outcome is that it never fills. That is intended and is not a failure.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is a low-beta industrial breaking out into a print in a tape where the economically sensitive names are being sold, and that the 1.4% ATR which makes the geometry look clean is the same thing that makes a 9.6% target slow and easy to stall out of. Answered with the relative-strength measurement rather than with a view: UNP has beaten its own sector over every window — 1m +0.86% against XLI -1.07%, 3m -4.34% against XLI -7.28%, 6m +15.48% against XLI -2.42%, so 17.9 points of 6-month outperformance against the sector and 5.5 against SPY. It is the leadership of the group, not a laggard being caught. And on 2026-10-14, the session that took CCJ -5.4%, CEG -5.5%, MU -4.1% and gold -1.5%, UNP closed +1.44% at a 10-week high.
